Matsu Meridian draws a comprehensive international compliance regime because it is a large, modern container vessel engaged in long-haul intercontinental trade (Asia–Europe). Built in 2019, it falls squarely within SOLAS Chapter II-1 scope for passenger and cargo ships over 500 GT, triggering full statutory survey and certification requirements. Its size (92,400 GT, 8,200 TEU) makes it subject to international conventions covering radiocommunications (GMDSS), navigational systems, and continuous synopsis records. Its fuel flexibility (HFO/VLSFO) and international trading area mandate MARPOL Annexes I through VI compliance, including oil record books, fuel oil consumption data collection (EU-MRV, MARPOL-VI-22A), operational carbon intensity rating, and NOx engine limits. The Singapore flag and European destination trigger Paris and Tokyo MoU port state control regimes. As an internationally trading vessel over 3,000 GT, it requires ballast water management, anti-fouling certification, maritime labour compliance, load line and tonnage certificates, and bunker/wreck removal insurance. The 2019 build date places it within modern construction standards requiring full ISPS-A security protocols and comprehensive hazardous materials documentation.

The Matsu Kestrel is a Panama-flagged container vessel built in 2008 with a gross tonnage of 13,760 and capacity of 1,118 TEU, operating in intra-Asia waters. This profile triggers comprehensive international maritime regulations because it is a commercial cargo vessel subject to SOLAS, MARPOL, ISPS, and other international conventions applicable to all ships of this size and type engaged in international trade. The container ship classification combined with its size (>5,000 GT) and commercial operation triggers the full suite of safety, security, environmental, and labor certification requirements.

The Matsu Solace draws this comprehensive 32-obligation set primarily due to its classification as a chemical/products tanker built in 2021 with a gross tonnage of 29,900. As a tanker vessel trading internationally in the Middle East–India region under Marshall Islands flag, it is subject to the full suite of SOLAS safety, ISPS security, and MARPOL pollution prevention requirements. The tanker type specifically triggers additional MARPOL Annex I (oil) and Annex II (noxious liquid substances) obligations including cargo record books, NLS certification, and specialized operational procedures. The post-2020 build year and HFO/VLSFO fuel type activate MARPOL Annex VI climate and emissions requirements including CII carbon intensity rating, fuel consumption data collection, and sulphur content monitoring. The vessel's size (29,900 GT) and international trading pattern place it under full ballast water management requirements, maritime labour certification, load line certification, anti-fouling system controls, and modern wreck removal and bunker liability insurance obligations. Together, these attributes—tanker type, recent construction, international trading, and fuel specification—establish the complete regulatory profile expected of a contemporary chemical tanker in global trade.

Matsu Cordillera draws this comprehensive 30-obligation set primarily because it is a large (44,100 GT) modern bulk carrier built in 2015 engaging in international transpacific trade. As a cargo ship of significant size, it triggers the full suite of SOLAS safety and ISPS security requirements, MARPOL pollution prevention certificates across all five annexes (oil, noxious liquids, sewage, garbage, and air pollution), ballast water management (BWM), maritime labour (MLC), anti-fouling (AFS), and load line provisions. Its 2015 build year makes it subject to contemporary standards including CII carbon intensity tracking, SEEMP energy efficiency requirements, bunker delivery note procedures, and fuel oil consumption data reporting under MARPOL VI. The vessel's use of HFO/VLSFO and diesel propulsion specifically triggers NOx emission limits and sulphur content regulation. Its international flag (Liberia) and transpacific trading pattern ensure application of port state control readiness standards (Tokyo MoU). The combination of bulk carrier classification, deadweight exceeding typical thresholds, and post-2012/2013 regulatory entry date collectively explains why substantially all general maritime instruments apply to this hull.

Annual Fire Main Systems and Equipment Test Survey Report — Inspect and test all fire mains, pumps, hydrants, hoses and portable extinguishers; document condition and readiness.
Fire Detection System Maintenance Test Log — Run fire detection system tests per maintenance schedule; record all results and any faults in log.
Abandon Ship and Fire Drill Report — Conduct abandon ship and fire drills with all crew members; document participants and results.

Annual Internal ISM Audit and Management Review Certificate — Conduct annual internal ISM audit and management review; document corrective actions required.
Quarterly Ship Security Drill Report — Conduct quarterly ship security drill with all personnel; document completion and findings.
Ship Security Certificate Verification Certificate — Schedule intermediate or renewal Ship Security Certificate verification with Singapore administration.
Annual IOPP Certificate Survey Report — Schedule and conduct annual IOPP Certificate survey with class surveyor; verify Supplement matches equipment.
Bilge Discharge 15 ppm Filter Equipment Test Survey Report — Test machinery space bilge discharge through 15 ppm filter equipment; verify alarm and auto-stop function.
Oil Record Book Part I and Crew Briefing Record — Verify Oil Record Book Part I current and ready; brief crew on recording requirements for next operation.
Fuel Oil Sample Analysis Report — Obtain and analyse fuel oil sample from next bunker delivery; verify sulphur content ≤0.50% globally.
Annual Fuel Consumption and Distance Data Analysis Report — Collect annual fuel consumption, distance and hours data; prepare report for Singapore MPA submission.
Crew Competency Certificates Verification Certificate — Verify all crew hold valid competency certificates for rank and ship type before next departure.
